_comment: Turkish words without their own TİD sign that are signed with an existing sign of the same meaning: word -> gloss of that sign. Read by isharati.lexicon.turkish.TIDLexicon.load_synonyms; a word is resolved through an entry here only after its exact form and its zeyrek lemma found no sign (the matcher never guesses a stem for a word the analyser knows, so «kulluk» cannot become «kul»). Keys are compared with Turkish casing and circumflex folded, as the word itself or its best lemma. Every entry is reviewed for meaning in Qur'an and hadith Turkish (Diyanet style); a word that gets its own sign later keeps that sign, and an entry whose target is not signed does nothing. Left out on purpose: ilah (a god, not Allah: 'there is no ilah but Allah'), tanrı (1 use, 'gods'), mevla (also 'freed slave / patron' in hadith), salat (here salawat on the Prophet, not namaz), azap -> ceza and sadaka -> infak (near-synonyms whose meaning differs), emretmek -> emir (the sign's sense, command or commander, is unknown), uçmak (the gloss is 'to fly'). zekât has no sign to map to. The signs stay pending Deaf review like their targets. Multi-word keys are fixed formulas signed by one sign (sallallahu aleyhi ve sellem -> ALEYHİSSELAM): they become phrase glosses of that sign, so the formula is matched and signed once.

_notes.rabbi: zeyrek's lemma of Rabb-forms (Rabbin, Rabbimiz): the same word Rab, which has its own sign
_notes.rableri: their Lord (Rab + plural possessive), unanalysed form
_notes.rasul: messenger of God; Diyanet usage = peygamber (the user's example)
_notes.rasulallah: vocative spelling of Rasûlullah (ey Allah'ın Rasûlü)
_notes.allahu: Arabic case form of Allah in formulas (Allahu Teâlâ, Allahu a'lem)
_notes.allahumme: 'O Allah', the vocative of Allah in supplications
_notes.tevbesini: inflected tevbe, unknown to the analyser
_notes.cami: mosque; the TİD sign for a mosque is used for both words
_notes.hacc: Arabic-style spelling of hac (pilgrimage), haccı / hacca
_notes.iblis: Iblis is the proper name of Satan, the being the şeytan sign names
_notes.firdevs: Firdevs is the highest garden of Paradise (cennetü'l-firdevs)
_notes.sahabe: the Companions; ashab is the same word's Arabic plural
_notes.vakit: time (beş vakit namaz, o vakit = then); same meaning as zaman
_notes.birlikte: together; AUTSL's beraber sign is glossed 'together'
_notes.yemin: oath; the sign is the act of swearing an oath
_notes.sabır: patience; the verb's sign, same root and meaning
_notes.dilemek: to will / ask for (Allah dilerse, rahmet dile); istemek = want / ask for
_notes.demek: to say (dedi ki); söylemek = to say / tell
_notes.sallallahu aleyhi ve sellem: the blessing formula after the Prophet's name (Arabic صلى الله عليه وسلم): one fixed formula, signed by the ALEYHİSSELAM sign
_notes.aleyhisselam: the formula 'peace be upon him' written as one word: the ALEYHİSSELAM sign
_notes.radıyallahu anh: 'may Allah be pleased with him' after a Companion's name: one formula, the ALLAH RAZI OLSUN sign
_notes.radıyallahu anha: the same formula for a woman (Aişe, Fatıma)
_notes.radıyallahu anhuma: the same formula for two people
_notes.radıyallahu anhum: the same formula for a group
_notes.dördüncü: ordinal without its own TİD sign: signed with its number's sign (ikinci and üçüncü have their own signs); pending Deaf review
